newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ingush refugees killed in North Ossetia attack.
newsitem.headline: Ingush refugees killed in North Ossetia attack.

text.p: An unspecified number of Ingush refugees returning to Russia's North Ossetia region were killed and at least 10 wounded when their bus was fired on with grenade launchers on Thursday, an Ingush presidential spokesman said.

"We have no information on how many were killed, but 10 people were sent to hospital in serious condition," Manlis Chakhkiyev, a spokesman for Ingushetia's President Ruslan Aushev, told Reuters by telephone. He said the bus carried 15 or 16 refugees. It was not clear who carried out the attack.
Interfax news agency quoted Ingush Interior Ministry officials as saying at least two people died in the attack, which took place only 15 km (10 miles) from the Ingush border.

More than 20 attacks against Ingush refugees returning to their homes in the Progorodny district, which is controlled by North Ossetia, have been committed in the last month, raising ethnic tension in Russia's turbulent North Caucasus region.
The Ingush side pinned the blame for the attacks on North Ossetians. An armed conflict between North Ossetia and Ingushetia in 1992 killed about 200 and sparked a huge flow of refugees.

Aushev sent a cable to Russian President Boris Yeltsin earlier this week warning him that tensions with the neighbouring region had increased sharply. He said direct presidential rule in the region could help in solving the problem.
